entities.name: Menedemus the Cynic
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Menedemus was a Cynic philosopher, and a pupil of the Epicurean Colotes of Lampsacus. Diogenes Laërtius states that he used to go about garbed as a Fury, proclaiming himself a sort of spy from Hades:He assumed the garb of a Fury, and went about saying that he had come from Hades to take notice of all who did wrong, in order that he might descend there again and make his report to the deities who live in that country. And this was his dress: a tunic of a dark colour reaching to his feet, and a purple girdle round his waist, an Arcadian hat on his head with the twelve signs of the zodiac embroidered on it, tragic buskins, a preposterously long beard, and an ashen staff in his hand.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Menedemus' unique attire and self-proclaimed role as a 'spy from Hades' allowed him to critique societal norms and challenge conventional values, contributing to the Cynic philosophical movement.
